coverage_gaps: Trial registries are unavailable, so ongoing or unpublished human studies and registry-publication matching are outside scope.
Preprint routes are unavailable, so recent unreviewed mechanistic findings may be missed.
Citation-graph and DOI-metadata routes are unavailable, limiting systematic forward and backward citation expansion beyond records discoverable in PubMed.
Regulatory, patent, chemistry, and non-PubMed subject-index routes are unavailable, so translational safety actions, prior art, and records indexed only elsewhere are not covered.
PubMed indexing and abstract availability may underrepresent older, non-English, conference, or very recent online-first evidence.
exclusion_criteria: Studies mentioning LRRK2 or Parkinson disease only incidentally without direct genetic, mechanistic, substrate, physiological, or limitation evidence.

Substrate claims based solely on overexpression, motif prediction, or a single unvalidated in vitro assay when no direct phosphorylation evidence is reported; such records may remain navigation leads but cannot support a physiological-substrate conclusion.
Disease studies unrelated to Parkinson disease or parkinsonism unless they directly inform LRRK2 enzymatic mechanism, substrate biology, or context dependence.
Commentaries, news items, and unsourced narrative opinions used as claim evidence.
Duplicate publications reporting the same cohort or experiment without additional decision-relevant data.
Records whose available language, abstract, or full-text information is insufficient for reliable eligibility assessment after feasible translation checks.
inclusion_criteria: PubMed-indexed records published on or before 2024-12-31; apply the cutoff after retrieval when online-first and issue dates are ambiguous.
Primary human linkage, pedigree, segregation, association, ancestry, founder, or penetrance studies that directly evaluate LRRK2 in Parkinson disease or parkinsonism.
Biochemical, structural, cellular, or animal studies that directly test LRRK2 kinase or GTPase activity, disease-variant effects, substrate phosphorylation, or downstream physiology.

Substrate studies with direct phosphorylation evidence and studies using endogenous proteins, physiological expression, genetic perturbation, or orthogonal validation; retain weaker substrate evidence with an explicit evidence-strength label.
Null, negative, conflicting, replication, loss-of-function, correction, and retraction records relevant to the proposed genetic or enzymatic mechanism.
Reviews and meta-analyses used for terminology expansion, evidence mapping, and citation navigation, with mechanistic claims traced to primary records.
Records in any language when an English abstract or usable translation permits eligibility assessment and accurate extraction.
Deduplicate canonical records by PMID and DOI while preserving every query-to-record occurrence and retrieval-wave provenance.

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: in familial and sporadic Parkinson disease, trace LRRK2 genetic discovery, segregation and association of disease-linked variants, penetrance and population effects, kinase and GTPase mechanisms, endogenous physiological substrates, downstream cellular phenotypes, and null, negative, conflicting, or context-limiting evidence. Search PubMed from database inception through 2024-12-31, include human studies and informative biochemical, cellular, and animal models, consider all languages when an English abstract or usable translation is available, prioritize primary studies for claims, and use reviews for terminology and citation navigation.
stop_rules: Do not exceed 12 query events, and stop routine retrieval once all planned events have been executed through the 2024-12-31 cutoff.

Verify that sentinel retrieval recovers primary genetic-discovery and Rab-substrate anchor study classes; if either check fails, use only remaining query events to revise aliases and report any unresolved recall failure.

Require eligible primary evidence for genetic discovery, disease-associated variants, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates, and at least one mechanism-limiting category before declaring thematic coverage complete.

Stop further terminology or citation expansion after two consecutive screened result batches add no new eligible variant, catalytic relationship, physiological substrate, downstream phenotype, or limitation evidence.

Before stopping, deduplicate by PMID and DOI, preserve all query-to-record links, and record each query, execution timestamp, result count, requested cutoff, and available provider-version information.
Stop earlier if remaining PubMed retrieval cannot plausibly change the brief's confidence or scope; document the rationale and unresolved coverage gaps.
If the query-event budget is exhausted before thematic saturation, stop and report budget exhaustion together with the uncovered evidence dimensions.
